newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy on course to meet deficit/GDP goal - Ciampi.
newsitem.headline: Italy on course to meet deficit/GDP goal - Ciampi.

text.p: Italy is on course to cut its deficit to three percent of GDP in 1997, fulfilling a key requirement for countries wishing to join the single European currency, Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said.
"The performance of state accounts over recent months are in line with reaching the (three percent) objective," Ciampi told a joint sitting of the parliament's two budget commissions.
"We will only know if we have reached three percent on December 31, but I have faith we will do it," Ciampi said.
Italy's deficit was 6.7 percent of GDP in 1996.

Under the terms of the Maastricht Treaty countries wishing to sign up to European economic and monetary union (EMU) should have a deficit/GDP ratio of three percent or lower. Founder euro members are due to be chosen next May.
